strengths: The paper addresses an important deployment bottleneck: the cost of feeding numerous visual tokens into large language models. Combining CLS-attention-based selection with key-similarity-based merging provides a simple, plausible approach that preserves the existing backbone.

Reducing 576 visual tokens to approximately 40 is substantial. Evaluation covers six benchmarks and both 7B and 13B backbones. After fine-tuning, the 7B model preserves ScienceQA and POPE performance particularly well, demonstrating a potentially useful compression tradeoff.

The ablations provide encouraging evidence for the components. Adding token supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 in Table 4. Training-free PruMerge also achieves 54.00 on TextVQA, compared with at most 47.96 for the spatial-sampling configurations in Table 3.

The overall pipeline and visualizations are understandable. The manuscript attributes its backbone, training data, benchmarks, and methodological antecedents, and explicitly acknowledges lossy compression and limitations in model coverage.
weaknesses: Practical efficiency remains insufficiently validated. Section 4.2 and Table 2 explicitly report roofline estimates for LLM prefill under one assumed prompt length. There are no measured end-to-end latency or memory results incorporating vision encoding, selection, merging, and autoregressive decoding. The theoretical analysis supports potential savings, but does not establish the deployment benefits central to the contribution.

The comparisons do not adequately establish the advantage over existing token-reduction approaches. Table 3 primarily compares against retaining the first 40 tokens and uniform spatial sampling. Comparisons with the cited token-merging/pruning methods, and with fixed-budget top-k CLS-attention selection using the same merging and training procedure, are needed to isolate the contribution of the proposed combination and its adaptive rule.

Performance preservation is overstated. In Table 1, VQAv2 falls from 78.5 to 72.0 for 7B and from 80.0 to 72.8 for 13B; 7B MME falls from 1510.7 to 1350.3. Without fine-tuning, POPE falls from 85.9 to 76.2 in Table 5. These losses may be acceptable at such aggressive compression, but describing them as marginal or claiming no sacrifice of reasoning capabilities is insufficiently supported.

Important implementation details impede reproduction. Algorithm 1 replaces each selected center with an unnormalized weighted sum over other tokens, whereas the prose describes supplementing retained tokens through weighted averaging. Center inclusion, weight normalization, overlapping neighborhoods, the value of k, and attention-head aggregation need clarification. The LoRA configuration is also underspecified. These ambiguities affect the actual computation, beyond presentation alone.

The adaptive-budget claim has limited evidence. A few visualizations do not establish that IQR selection allocates an appropriate or 'optimal' number of tokens according to image complexity. Token-count distributions, threshold sensitivity, and accuracy-versus-budget curves are missing. Experiments are also confined to LLaVA-1.5 at 336×336 resolution, leaving the prominently motivated high-resolution and video applications unvalidated.
